title: Paged KV slab segmentation and GPU tail-swap protocol for continuous batching
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: As usage patterns skew toward long-context chat and embeddings with occasional bursts, our monolithic KV cache is causing inefficient GPU memory residency and jitter for continuous batching. This ticket proposes a slab-segmentation approach for the paged KV cache combined with a new "tail-swap" GPU swap protocol to reduce OOMs, lower tail latency, and improve steady-state token throughput without regressing P50 latency. Scope: implementation touches runtime cache allocator, GPU swap coordinator, and batching router. Excludes SDK changes and console UI (followups).
proposal: 1) Introduce segmented slab allocator: split KV space into fixed-size slabs (64KB, 256KB, 1MB) grouped by recent access recency to reduce fragmentation and allow block-aligned swaps. 2) Hot/Cool cohorts: assign slabs to hot or cool cohorts based on a lightweight LRU+frequency score computed at request enqueue time. 3) Tail-swap protocol: on GPU memory pressure, prefer swapping coolest slabs (chunk-aligned) and perform an asynchronous 'tail-swap' that writes contiguous slab ranges to preallocated backing store to avoid PCIe stalls. 4) Prefetch hints: integrate prefetch hinting from the batching router by sending predicted next-token kv ranges with low-priority prefetch channel. 5) Metrics & counters: track slab residency, swap latency distribution, and prefetch hit rate.
implementation_plan: - Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): implement allocator prototype in python runtime shim + unit tests to validate slab allocation/free patterns. - Phase 2 (Core, 3 weeks): C++ runtime implementation, GPU swap API, and backing store writer. - Phase 3 (Integration, 1 week): hook prefetch hints from batching router, end-to-end bench harness. - Phase 4 (Canary, 1 week): deploy to dedicated pool with synthetic long-context load and compare P50/P95/P99. - Phase 5 (Rollout): gated release with runtime-1.26. Concurrency: small feature-flag for slab segmentation and separate flag for tail-swap protocol.
benchmarks: Spike results (local dev rig, 8xA100): baseline steady-state throughput 72 tokens/sec per GPU; slab-segmentation + tail-swap prototype improved steady-state to 88 tokens/sec (+22%), reduced swap-induced P99 latency from 420ms to 160ms in oversubscription scenarios. Prefetch hit rate varied: 42% on deterministic prefix workloads, 18% on open-ended chat. These are preliminary; production canary needed.
decisions: Use fixed slab sizes to bound external fragmentation (64KB/256KB/1MB)
Implement tail-swap as a background, contiguous-writer process to minimize PCIe transactions
Prefetch hints will be best-effort and low-priority to avoid hurting foreground latency
alternatives_considered: Per-request variable-sized allocator: declined due to fragmentation and complex compaction cost
Full KV compaction background daemon: high CPU/backing-store IO cost and longer tail latencies
Page-granular swapping with fine-grain eviction: better utilization but caused high PCIe overhead in tests
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: tail-swap writer could contend for PCIe bandwidth and increase P50 if not throttled. Mitigation: add rate limiter and backpressure; start with conservative write window and increase via runtime flag. Risk: prefetch hints may pollute cache; mitigation: separate prefetch cohort and evict prefetch-only slabs first.
tests: Unit tests for allocator invariants, integration tests for swap correctness, synthetic stress tests simulating oversubscription, and a canary workload consisting of mixed short/long-context chat to validate P50/P95/P99 and throughput. Add test harness for measuring PCIe stall time via existing GPU telemetry hooks.
monitoring_and_rollout_strategy: Expose slab_residency_gauge, tail_swap_latency_histogram, prefetch_hit_ratio; create dashboard in Console with heatmap of cohort occupancy. Canary on a single dedicated pool; abort rollout if P99 latency increases >20% or OOMs do not drop after 30 minutes.
